subject: Residual access & service boundary inquiry — Aurora Health SOC2 evidence
messages:
From: Lina Morales <lina.morales@aurorahealth.com>
To: alex.martinez@redwood.com
Cc: security-audits@cloudplus.io
Date: 2026-01-07T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: SOC2 Type II evidence + clarification on residual access & subservice responsibilities

Hi Alex,

We are preparing for our external SOC2 Type II assessment (audit period: 2025-01-01 through 2025-12-31) and need to validate coverage for systems that process Aurora PHI and metadata. A few asks from our audit team: 

- Confirmation of Redwood's SOC2 Type II report for calendar year 2025, plus whether you will provide a bridge letter covering any gap between Redwood's report period and our auditor's window.
- Clarify subservice boundaries: specifically, how Redwood treats CloudPlus (our infra provider) in your scope — do you operate under a carve-out or is CloudPlus included as a subservice organization?
- Evidence: list of subprocessors, current KMS custody model (who holds encryption keys for customer data at rest and for backups), and any controls that limit residual access from cloud provider system admins.

Would you be able to provide the SOC report (redacted if necessary), a draft bridge letter, and a subprocessor CSV? Our auditor prefers documents by 2026-01-15 to align with interview scheduling. If you have standard language you expect us to accept around CloudPlus's SOC coverage, please surface that.

Thanks — Lina
Lina Morales
Senior Audit Manager, Aurora Health
lina.morales@aurorahealth.com
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Lina Morales <lina.morales@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: 2026-01-08T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: SOC2 Type II evidence + clarification on residual access & subservice responsibilities

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front and a proposed plan: 

1) SOC2 report: we can provide our SOC2 Type II report for the period ending 2025-12-31. We typically redact customer-specific schedules; if your auditor needs an unredacted copy we can discuss an NDA/execution path. Attached is a short SOC summary to speed review.

2) Bridge letter: we can draft a bridge letter confirming continuous controls between report issuance and the audit window where applicable. I will attach a draft for your team to review.

3) Subservice & CloudPlus: Redwood treats CloudPlus as a subservice provider for infrastructure. Our default model is a subservice inclusion (not a carve-out) for the compute/network/storage layer, but certain responsibilities (KMS key custody, backup snapshot retention and access) are shared — we control the application-level KMS keys by default, while CloudPlus has platform-level operational access for infrastructure maintenance. We can provide the CloudPlus SOC summary we rely on and a mapping of shared vs. Redwood-owned controls. Please let us know if Aurora's auditor requires a carve-out-style bridge letter instead of subservice inclusion.

4) Evidence: we will provide a current subprocessor list and a KMS custody statement. To confirm expectations: does your auditor need proof of HSM/KMS attestations (e.g., CloudPlus KMS SOC claims) or only product-level email attestation from Redwood?

Plan/timeline: we aim to deliver the SOC report summary, subprocessors CSV, and a bridge-letter draft by EOD 2026-01-12. If you need earlier delivery of any item, please flag the priority and we'll escalate.

Attachment: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (summary stub)

Regards,
Alex Martinez
Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: Lina Morales <lina.morales@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2026-01-10T14:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: SOC2 Type II evidence + clarification on residual access & subservice responsibilities

Alex — looping in a few details your auditor will likely ask for so we can include them in the package. Quoting Lina's request below for context.

On 2026-01-07, Lina Morales wrote:
> We are preparing for our external SOC2 Type II assessment (audit period: 2025-01-01 through 2025-12-31) ...

Key items I will add to the deliverables: 
- CloudPlus relationship doc (we'll include the CloudPlus SOC pointer and their latest subprocessor export). I requested their 2025 SOC summary and a CSV of subprocessors; pending receipt from their security-audits alias.
- KMS custody detail: Redwood uses customer-derived application-level keys stored in a managed KMS (AWS KMS/CloudPlus KMS integration) depending on deployment mode. For our hosted customers we maintain envelope encryption with keys in a Redwood-managed KMS tenant; for Dedicated and Private customers we offer bring-your-own-key. I will create a short 'KMS custody & key rotation' statement and include control references (access controls, key rotation cadence, HSM attestations if available).
- Residual access controls: I'll enumerate platform-level roles, break-glass controls, and the limited operational playbook that governs CloudPlus access.

Question for audit scoping: does Aurora require that CloudPlus be named as an included subservice org (auditor pulls CloudPlus SOC) or would a Redwood mapping + CloudPlus SOC pointer suffice? That changes the level of evidence we provide.

I'll aim to attach: cloudplus-subprocessors-2025.csv (if CloudPlus provides it), KMS-custody-statement.txt, and the bridge letter draft by 2026-01-12. If anyone on Redwood wants to review the KMS statement before we send, ping me.

— Soojin
